paper.title_en: Probing core excitation in the breakup of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> with state-of-the-art nuclear structure inputs
paper.abstract_en: The role of core excitation in the breakup of the proton-halo nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is investigated within a coupled-channels framework using microscopic nuclear structure inputs from Gamow shell model (GSM) calculations, which consistently incorporate many-body correlations and continuum coupling. The breakup reactions of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> on <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Zn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>64</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>120</mn></mmultiscripts></math> targets at incident energies near the Coulomb barriers were studied with the GSM-derived overlap functions, allowing a configuration-resolved assessment of the main components of the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> ground state. The results show that the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>7</mn></mmultiscripts></math>(<math><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>) <math><mo>⊗</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> configuration provides the dominant contribution to the inclusive breakup cross section. In addition, the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>7</mn></mmultiscripts></math>(<math><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>) <math><mo>⊗</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> configuration, often neglected in previous studies, contributes at the <math><mo>∼</mo><mn>10</mn></math>% level, while the core-excited <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>7</mn></mmultiscripts></math>(<math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>) <math><mo>⊗</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> configuration accounts for about 20% of the total breakup yield. Including these additional configurations leads to a substantially improved description of the measured angular distributions. Sensitivity tests with respect to the optical potentials and nuclear-structure input indicate that these conclusions are robust. The corresponding dynamical polarization potentials show that core excitation enhances both the repulsive real part and the absorptive imaginary part of the breakup-induced polarization potential. These results demonstrate that, although the breakup of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is governed primarily by the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">Be</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>⊗</mo><mo> </mo><mi>p</mi></math> halo configurations, core excitation provides a quantitatively important contribution and should be included in realistic descriptions of near-barrier breakup observables.
